s: The most widespread forests in India are:

s: Which one among the following covers the highest percentage of forest area in the world?
x:
Most books and the UPSC 2003 key: temperate coniferous forests (taiga). Strictly, FAO FRA 2020 ranks the tropical domain first (Tropical > Boreal > Temperate > Subtropical), though that includes tropical dry forests, not only rain forests (PMF Indian Physical Geography 03 p.64).
Most books and the official key take the vast coniferous (taiga) belt of Eurasia and North America as the largest share of world forest. FAO puts the tropical domain first, but that counts all tropical forests, not just rain forests.

s: In India, which type of forest among the following occupies the largest area?
x: Among the options, tropical moist deciduous forests are by far the largest (18.47% of forest cover, ISFR 2021). Montane wet temperate (2.83%), wet evergreen (2.74%) and sub-tropical dry evergreen (0.02%) are small; the larger dry deciduous type is not offered.
